groups.text: It is currently cloudy and 25 degrees Celsius in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

In Germany, a political "firewall" continues to block the far-right Alternative for Germany party from joining any state or federal government. Despite establishing itself as a significant political force over the last thirteen years, the anti-immigrant AfD remains excluded from power by this agreement against cooperation. Separately, the European technology sector has seen its largest equity fundraising round ever. Mistral AI announced it raised three billion euros in a Series D round, bringing the company's valuation to more than twenty-one billion euros. Samsung Electronics led the funding alongside PSG Equity and the Scaleup Europe Fund. Mistral intends to use the capital to expand compute capacity for training models and grow its international footprint. The company currently operates across twenty countries and provides AI transformation services for global enterprises including HSBC, ASML, and Airbus.

President Volodymyr Zelensky is giving cautious backing to peace proposals brought by U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. While he described the ideas as decent, Zelensky remains unsure if they can be effectively implemented. He highlighted grain and energy as sensitive issues for both Ukraine and Russia, including a proposal for a truce in aerial strikes against energy infrastructure that Russia has not yet accepted. This diplomatic effort comes as Russian drones continue to target civilian transport; a regional train on the Dnipro-Zaporizhzhia route was recently attacked, leaving one conductor out of contact. Zelensky hopes to meet President Donald Trump around September 20 to request more anti-ballistic missiles. Meanwhile, in a separate shift of wealth, hedge-fund billionaire Chris Rokos is leaving the UK for Greece. Ranked as Britain's third-largest taxpayer, Rokos plans to open an office in Athens to take advantage of Greece's flat tax on overseas income.

Twenty-six Filipino seafarers are awaiting repatriation after an attack on the bulk carrier Gingo while it was docked in Ukraine on September 2nd. The Department of Migrant Workers confirms all crew members disembarked safely by September 4th and remain unharmed, though they must first transit through Moldova to return home. Meanwhile, a coalition of 33 collectives and associations organizing technical events for developers is warning that their conferences are becoming economically unviable. These organizers cite falling ticket sales and reduced corporate sponsorship budgets, fearing that the loss of these community-driven events will impoverish the sector as companies lean more heavily on AI. This shift toward automation coincides with rising security concerns in the enterprise space. A virtual event hosted by Dark Reading highlights that while cloud adoption is increasing, many organizations are struggling to manage security risks and identify vulnerabilities within multi-cloud environments in the age of AI.

In Indonesia, the eruption of the volcanic island Anak Krakatau has caused flight cancellations at Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport. The airport has since reopened after the volcano began spewing ash and lava on September 4th. A Copernicus Sentinel-3 satellite captured images of the event, showing a white plume of water vapour, carbon dioxide, and sulphur dioxide alongside brown clouds of drifting debris. In Pakistan, the Islamabad High Court is forming a larger bench to hear a petition against a nationwide protest planned by the PTI for September 27th. The court noted the matter is sensitive with potential constitutional implications, while a local trader argues the demonstration could disrupt business and traffic in the capital. Meanwhile, in sports, Real Madrid faces Inter Milan today at the Santiago Bernabéu for the first round of the Champions League. The match begins at 16:00 Brasília time.

Benjamin Netanyahu faces intense pressure from Israeli opposition figures following a Haaretz investigation claiming he ignored an alert about the October 7 attacks. The report alleges that the President of the United Arab Emirates warned Netanyahu in late September 2023 that Hamas was preparing a major operation, but the Prime Minister did not inform security chiefs. While his cabinet rejects these accusations, the controversy comes as Israel approaches legislative elections. In Kenya, President William Ruto has ordered a crackdown on foreign nationals working as hawkers and petty retailers to reserve those low-capital businesses for Kenyan citizens. The government began enforcing this policy on September 7, sparking fears of xenophobia despite claims that documented traders remain protected. Meanwhile, Jose Olger Melo Charry, a Colombian soldier in the French Foreign Legion, has escaped captivity. He was taken hostage by a dissident FARC faction on August 6 and survived a four-day trek through rebel territory to reach freedom.

European manufacturers face a new regulatory burden starting September 11, as the Cyber Resilience Act enters its next phase. Under this law, companies must now report serious incidents and actively exploited vulnerabilities to ENISA, the European Union's central cybersecurity agency. This requirement applies to any business selling products with digital components, ranging from common devices to critical hardware like smart meter gateways. While these regulations tighten oversight in Europe, enterprises globally are struggling to secure their own internal systems. Many organizations are currently scrambling to balance operational power with security as they integrate AI into their corporate strategies. Meanwhile, the physical risks to media infrastructure remain acute in Eastern Europe. Russian forces recently attacked the offices of the My-Ukraine and My-Ukraine+ television channels, striking the newsroom and staff offices and leaving several people wounded.

In India, experts warn that proposed age assurance rules for child safety may inadvertently block adults from essential digital public services, as many citizens rely on their children to navigate state portals. This tension over platform access comes as India weighs age-gating and design duties ahead of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act's child data provisions taking effect in May 2027. Meanwhile, environmental risks are mounting in the Himalayas, where rising temperatures drive glacier retreat and create unstable glacial lakes. These conditions contributed to an August 2026 disaster in Nepal, where a massive mountain slope failure in Langtang National Park sent debris and floodwaters nearly 100 kilometers downstream. In separate industrial news, Samsung Electronics and ASML are expanding their partnership to advance High NA EUV lithography. Samsung plans to transition from traditional 6-inch photomasks to 12-inch technology and introduce these tools into DRAM high-volume manufacturing by 2028.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with temperatures between 19 and 28 degrees Celsius.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your work calendar has a NAS Sync at two in the afternoon and a RAYX Meeting at three. Your personal calendar has Krebs starting at six in the evening.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
